localFacts.fact: funda's article for estate agents on 360° photos says distortion often comes from the camera moving between frames, so always use a tripod to keep the camera still.
Photofacts (Liesbeth van Asselt) gives the rule of thumb that camera plus lens should weigh at most half the tripod's load capacity; the post's own mark is three times.
Dutch terms: tandwielkop / geared head, 3-wegkop, balhoofd, snelkoppelingsplaat, waterpas, L-beugel; Arca-Swiss keeps its name.

localPainPoints.pain: A ball head sags a little after locking, which spoils a carefully levelled frame.
localPainPoints.fix: A geared head moves each axis by knob and holds the position (geared vs ball section).

quotes.text: dan zakt de camera altijd nog iets door na het vastzetten van het balhoofd. Dus daar gaat je compositie.
Als je niet wilt dat je statiefkop nog even zakt, moet je een geared head nemen.

localGain.point: Photofacts' Dutch voice on sagging ball heads, answered with the geared head.
funda's always-a-tripod advice for 360° photos, tied to the HDR/bracketing stability point.
Photofacts' half-the-load rule next to the post's 3x headroom column.
